title.narrative: SEPA, Environmental Governance in the Mining Sector, 2022-2026

description.narrative:
Cooperation between Swedish Environmental Protection Agency, SMHI and SGU, and Zambian authorities and organisations on environmental governance and implementation of Zambias National Adaptation Plan, with focus on mining.
The Swedish Environmental Protection Agency (SEPA) and partners (Swedish Geological Survey, SGU, Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute, SMHI) have presented a proposal for an intervention focusing on integrating environment, climate and human rights to mining governance. The partners will cooperate closely with partners in Zambia, including the United Nations Development Programme in Zambia, UNDP Zambia, Diakonia, Action Aid Zambia, Transparency International Zambia and Global Water Partnership., GWP. The Ministry of Green Economy and Environment (MoGEE) will together with the Zambian Environmental Management Agency, ZEMA, be SEPAs main counterpart in the Zambian administration. SEPA and the project team will also engage with the Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development, industry organisations like Zambia Chamber of Mines, and other industry representatives.SEPA, SMHI and SGU are Swedish authorities, representing the Swedish public administration model, and are all engaged in development cooperation with support from Sida. SEPA is an active member in the Public Agency Hub and a central assessment of SEPA has been undertaken.UNDP globally and UNDP Zambia already cooperates with SEPA within the global Environmental Governance Programme (EGP) since 2014 which focus on integrating environment and human Rights into the governance of the mining sector. Diakonia in Zambia works to strengthen accountability in communities in natural resource rich areas.The proposed programme builds on earlier cooperation and experiences, including SEPA collaboration with UNDP, SMHI International Training Programmes (ITPs) on climate change, SGU ITPs on mine water and mine waste management, and Diakonia's activities in Zambia. The programme will address the following areas:-licensing and permitting process of large scale mining operations as well as awareness raising-knowledge generation and strategic planning related to climate change issues connected to mining-enhancement of the national discourse on sustainable mining by gathering strategic actors to highlight and amass joint pressure on certain "hot topics" related to the Zambian mining sector -provide channels for Zambian actors within the mining value chain to access and interact with regional and global platforms with similar aims as the programmeThe draft agreement follows the agreed Sida templates for General and Specific Conditions for Grants to Swedish Governmental Authorities.

Samarbete med Naturvårdsverket , SMHI och SGU med zambiska myndigheter och organisationer om hållbar förvaltning av gruvsektorn samt genomförande av Zambias klimatanpassningsplan med fokus på gruvdrift,

The overall objective of the contribution is to strengthen capacity of the Zambian partners to implement sustainable mining governance which integrates environment and human rights. The program works through three components:
Component 1: Support to development of consultation, examination, and supervision - the mining licensing process The aim of this component is to strengthen the procedures and processes in selected steps of the mining licensing cycle. The process is to include regards to environment and human rights relating to mining by using the Swedish environmental permitting procedure as a reference. SGU will co-lead this together with SEPA.
Component 2: Stakeholder coordination forum This component will enable interactions with different interest and gather strategic actors in dialogue. The intention is to highlight and amass joint pressure on certain identified hot topics related to the Zambian mining sector. The component will also provide coordination opportunities between government bodies currently holding responsibilities governing the mining sector. Component 3: Support to Zambia's efforts in addressing mining and climate change effects SMHI will co-lead this together with SEPA. This component would focus on providing a systemic understanding of links between climate change and the mining sector and also possibly aim to formulate support activities integrating mining issues and measures to the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) where this knowledge is deemed insufficient. In the continuation, the programme aims to collaborate with local partners to formulate pilot activities/ small projects intended to offer tools to support implementation of the NAP in relation to the mining sector and increase the general understanding of the mining sector of challenges and opportunities in a transition towards carbon neutrality. Pilot activities will be designed to be possible to implement within the ZAMNEX initiative and the authorities/actors existing organisations mandate and resources.

title.narrative: SEPA, Environmental Governance in the Mining Sector
SEPA, Environmental Governance in the Mining Sector

description.narrative:
In 2024, ZAMNEX transitioned from the inception phase to implementing targeted interventions to improve governance in Zambia's mining sector, guided by a newly finalized strategic direction and stakeholder-informed priorities. The programme also focused on building stakeholder capacity and promoting knowledge sharing, ensuring that implementation was grounded in current research and best practices.
The following are some notable results achieved:
Baseline studies completed (all components) - In 2024, ZAMNEX conducted baseline studies across all three programme components to assess the current state of governance in Zambia's mining sector, identify knowledge gaps, and inform the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) framework. Using a harmonized methodology that combined surveys and in-depth interviews, the studies provided a shared understanding among stakeholders and introduced initial strategic recommendations. As a result, the finalized baseline reports became foundational tools for guiding implementation, aligning stakeholder perspectives, and supporting long-term institutional learning and policy development.
Study visit to Sweden and targeted training in impact-based warnings - In August 2024, ZAMNEX facilitated a study visit to Sweden for the Zambia Meteorological Department (ZMD) and the Water Resources Management Authority (WARMA), where participants received targeted training from the Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute (SMHI) on developing impact-based warning systems. The activity enhanced the institutions capacity to utilize their data for generating timely and reliable climate warnings tailored to Zambia's mining sector, especially in response to extreme weather events like the 2024 drought. As a result, ZMD and WARMA gained practical knowledge, identified data management gaps, and strengthened regional collaboration with Zimbabwean counterparts to improve resilience and early warning systems.
Mine closure training in Kitwe - The mine closure training held in Kitwe aimed to enhance stakeholder capacity in planning, monitoring, and managing mine closures by integrating local and international expertise. As a result, participants from diverse sectors significantly improved their knowledge, clarified stakeholder consultation roles, and proposed collaborative strategies for more transparent and sustainable mine closure processes, ultimately benefiting government agencies, academia, industry, and environmental organizations involved in Zambia's mining sector.
Kickoff Workshop for National CSR Guiding Framework - The Kickoff Workshop for the National Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Guiding Framework under ZAMNEX Component 2 aimed to raise awareness of Strategic Corporate Responsibility (SCR) in Zambia and validate the development process for national CSR guidelines. As a result, key stakeholders from government, private sector, academia and civil society increased their understanding of CSR, endorsed the platforms recommendations, and committed to collaboratively shaping a national framework aligned with international best practices. Extensive literature review was conducted to increase stakeholder awareness of Strategic Corporate Responsibility (SCR) in Zambia by analyzing national legal frameworks and international best practices relevant to CSR, particularly in the mining sector. The findings filled a critical knowledge gap, informed the development of Zambias National CSR Guiding Framework, and benefited a wide range of stakeholders, including government, private sector, civil society, and development partners. This provided accessible, evidence-based insights into effective CSR implementation.
Finalising the ZAMNEX results framework and monitoring and evaluation framework - The ZAMNEX programme was developed through a highly participatory process involving Zambian stakeholders, resulting in the co-creation of a Theory of Change (ToC), Outcome Framework (OF), and Monitoring and Evaluation System (MEL). During its inception year in 2023, the programme focused on refining these frameworks using insights from baseline studies, ensuring strong stakeholder ownership and a robust foundation for implementation and impact measurement.
As ZAMNEX evolved into a fully operational programme, it integrated cross-cutting themes such as gender equality, anti-corruption, and poverty reduction into its core objectives, with a strong emphasis on transparency, equitable resource distribution, and inclusive governance in the mining sector. While challenges remain in achieving gender balance due to structural and procedural constraints, ZAMNEX has actively engaged strategic partners and civil society organizations to strengthen gender competence, foster inclusive participation, and promote conflict prevention through dialogue, trust-building, and collaboration. This complemented efforts with the Environmental Governance Programme (EGP) to enhance mining governance in Zambia.
